column1: # expect.tsv — the sentinel expectations of test/sliceflowsenscheck.sh, WRITTEN BEFORE the flow-sensitive
# walk existed (docs/EVALS.md, "Flow-sensitive slice in the small"). One row per USE row (k=use|both) of the
# sliced variable: rd = the exact set of def LINES that reach that use under the registered rule (comma
# list ascending, "-" = none inside the definition). reason = required exactly when the source-order
# (name-based) rule's edge DISAPPEARS under the flow-sensitive one: exit=K (the def's path leaves through
# the jump at line K before the use), branch=K (the branch head at line K puts the def on a sibling path), or
# unit=K (the statement starting at line K folds the def and the use into ONE unit — a nested def/lambda/class
# body — so the use reads the state entering that statement), or try=K (the try at line K: its handler sees
# the state BEFORE each statement of the body, so the body's last def never reaches the handler). The gate
# re-derives the source-order edge from the tool's own rows and checks K sits where the reason says
# (exit/branch: strictly between the vanished def and the use; unit/try: at or before the def, before the
# use) and reads as that kind of statement in the source.
